content: 1. The body of the equipment must display clear instructions warning operators not to leave the fogger unattended while it is in operation. 2. Portable thermal foggers must meet specific requirements, including compliance with the use of austenitic steel No. 4845, and manufacturers must provide a certificate confirming this compliance. 3. The weight of the equipment, when filled to the manufacturer’s maximum recommended capacity, must not exceed 20 kg. 4. The pesticide tank may be fixed or detachable, and its capacity must be clearly indicated. If the tank is not translucent and graduated, a means of measuring the liquid volume, such as a dipstick, must be provided. 5. For permanently fixed tanks, the filler opening must be on the top, and a filter funnel must be provided if the opening is less than 90 mm. If the opening is in a different position, an angled filter funnel must be supplied. 6. The fuel tank must have sufficient capacity to allow continuous discharge of a full pesticide tank at the minimum recommended flow rate without refilling. Fuel and pesticide tanks must not be refilled while the equipment is hot, and the type of fuel must be clearly indicated on the unit. The fuel cap must be leak-proof. 7. The engine of a pulse-jet fogger must start with fewer than 15 strokes if using a manual pump or within 30 seconds if using an automatic electrically operated pump. 8. Flow rate control to the nozzle must be achieved through a fixed but interchangeable restrictor or a control valve. The flow rate for each setting must be marked on the machine or declared in the user manual. A manually operated on/off valve must be present, and an automatic cut-off switch must prevent pesticide flow to the nozzle when the engine stops. 9. The output of the fogging equipment must not increase due to erosion by more than 10%. 10. The droplet size for space treatments must have a volume median diameter (VMD) of less than 30 µm for oiland/or water-based formulations. For water-based larvicide sprays, the fogger must have a separate orifice/attachment to produce larger droplet sizes up to 100 µm. 11. A single strap must be provided for carrying the equipment. 12. The equipment must pass a durability test, operating for 50 hours without failure or difficulty restarting the engine. This test involves intermittent liquid flow interruptions every 15 minutes. 13. If the noise level exceeds 85 decibels, the equipment must be permanently labeled to indicate the need for ear protection. During street operations, the noise level must not exceed 100 decibels at a distance of one meter from the machine. 14. The user manual must include clear safety instructions warning operators never to leave the equipment unattended during operation due to the high risk of fire. 15. When using water-based fogging formulations, pulse-jet engines with a minimum of 24 horsepower (approximately 2 L/h fuel consumption) may be used. Adjuvants such as polyalcohols (glycol, glycerine) or emulsifying oils may be added to retard evaporation and improve pesticide dilution/emulsion in water. 16. Vehicle-mounted thermal foggers must be designed for outdoor space treatments, leaving no residual spray deposit. They must be mounted on a corrosion-resistant frame suitable for a truck and include a pesticide tank, an additional tank for flushing the system, or a pump system with a reverse function for automatic suction of remaining liquid. 17. The equipment must have a control system operable from the vehicle cabin, a fuel tank with sufficient capacity to empty a full pesticide tank during operation, and all tanks must be permanently marked and equipped with drainage facilities. 18. The engine exhaust and moving parts must be guarded to prevent injury. 19. The pesticide tank capacity must be at least 50 liters. If the tank is not translucent and graduated, a metering device must be provided to measure liquid volume. The tank cap must not leak during movement over rough terrain, and a filter funnel must be supplied for filling without spillage. 20. The type of fuel must be clearly indicated on the filler cap. 21. The fogging equipment must have a manual flow control device with fixed settings, and the flow rates for each setting must be listed in the manual. The minimum possible flow rate must also be specified. 22. A cut-off valve must automatically close when any part of the equipment is turned off or ceases to function. If a pressure system above 50 kPa is used, an automatic pressure release device must be fitted. 23. The nozzle must deliver droplets no larger than 30 µm VMD for space sprays. For larvicidal applications, a special design must allow droplet sizes up to 100 µm. 24. The remote control panel in the vehicle cabin must have permanently labeled switches for independently turning the machine and pesticide flow on and off. The design must ensure that pesticide does not enter the vehicle cabin. 25. The equipment must operate without failure or difficulty restarting the engine for at least 50 hours within two weeks, including an 8-hour test. Fuel and formulation lines, pumps, and other components must withstand durability tests without leakage. 26. Aerosol dispensers used for aircraft disinsection must comply with international specifications, including WHO guidelines for pre-flight, blocks-away, and top-of-descent techniques. 27. Both single-use and multi-use aerosol dispensers are used for aircraft disinsection. Single-use dispensers discharge all contents in one continuous spray, while multi-use dispensers require continuous nozzle depression for discharge. 28. Aerosol dispensers must be non-refillable, with a capacity specified by the purchasing agency. They must comply with government and IATA regulations for restricted articles by air. 29. The aerosol spray must be non-flammable, non-toxic, non-irritant, and non-injurious to aircraft materials. The finished product must be clean, uniform, and free from defects such as sediment or foreign particles. 30. The metal container should ideally be constructed in one piece without side or bottom seams. The container must be clearly marked with the percentage of active ingredients, net weight, expiry date, batch number, and mandatory health and safety information. 31. The product formulations must comply with the International Health Regulations (IHR, 2005) and use a non-flammable propellant with low global warming potential. 32. The dip tube must touch the bottom of the container and be effectively sealed to the valve to ensure discharge only through the valve orifice. 33. The valve must be designed to prevent reclosure or interruption of flow once opened. 34. A valve cap must fully cover the external portion of the valve to protect against accidental damage or discharge. It must be rigid and have a clearance of at least 3 mm above the valve. 35. The packaging must display product name, active substance weight percentage, number of units, batch number, health and safety information, and applicable transport information. 36. The aerosol must meet physical requirements, with no more than 20% of droplets exceeding 30 µm in diameter and no more than 1% exceeding 50 µm. 37. The dispenser must pass heat stability tests, showing no leakage or defects when exposed to 54°C. 38. Aircraft manufacturers and operators require aerosol dispensers to be certified according to AMS 1450 or Boeing D6-7127 specifications to ensure compatibility with aircraft materials. 39. The efficacy of insecticide products used in aircraft must be tested according to established guidelines, including droplet size determination and rough usage tests. 40. The dispenser must withstand a drop test from 75 cm onto a hardwood surface without leakage or damage. 41. The dispenser must pass a heat-stability test by immersion in a 60°C water bath for 3 minutes, with no leakage or defects.
